# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1708
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1708
- **Title**: fix(1706): codex auth single provider identity + full model list
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1706-codex-auth-provider-naming` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +342
- **Deletions**: -151
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1708
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1708
- **Title**: fix(1706): codex auth single provider identity + full model list
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1706-codex-auth-provider-naming` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +342
- **Deletions**: -151
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

AGENTS.md updated: the ChatGPT OAuth contract (one identity per auth domain, rename keeps the entry) and the model-list dispatch (codex `/models` + bundled synced catalog for the chatgpt-codex kind).

- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

AGENTS.md updated: the ChatGPT OAuth contract (one identity per auth domain, rename keeps the entry) and the model-list dispatch (codex `/models` + bundled synced catalog for the chatgpt-codex kind).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1708
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1708
- **Title**: fix(1706): codex auth single provider identity + full model list
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1706-codex-auth-provider-naming` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +342
- **Deletions**: -151
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

AGENTS.md updated: the ChatGPT OAuth contract (one identity per auth domain, rename keeps the entry) and the model-list dispatch (codex `/models` + bundled synced catalog for the chatgpt-codex kind).

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1708
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1708
- **Title**: fix(1706): codex auth single provider identity + full model list
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1706-codex-auth-provider-naming` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +342
- **Deletions**: -151
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

AGENTS.md updated: the ChatGPT OAuth contract (one identity per auth domain, rename keeps the entry) and the model-list dispatch (codex `/models` + bundled synced catalog for the chatgpt-codex kind).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1708
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1708
- **Title**: fix(1706): codex auth single provider identity + full model list
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1706-codex-auth-provider-naming` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +342
- **Deletions**: -151
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

AGENTS.md updated: the ChatGPT OAuth contract (one identity per auth domain, rename keeps the entry) and the model-list dispatch (codex `/models` + bundled synced catalog for the chatgpt-codex kind).

Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Title**: fix(1706): codex auth single provider identity + full model list
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1706-codex-auth-provider-naming` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +342
- **Deletions**: -151
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

AGENTS.md updated: the ChatGPT OAuth contract (one identity per auth domain, rename keeps the entry) and the model-list dispatch (codex `/models` + bundled synced catalog for the chatgpt-codex kind).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1708
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1708
- **Title**: fix(1706): codex auth single provider identity + full model list
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1706-codex-auth-provider-naming` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +342
- **Deletions**: -151
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

AGENTS.md updated: the ChatGPT OAuth contract (one identity per auth domain, rename keeps the entry) and the model-list dispatch (codex `/models` + bundled synced catalog for the chatgpt-codex kind).

- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

AGENTS.md updated: the ChatGPT OAuth contract (one identity per auth domain, rename keeps the entry) and the model-list dispatch (codex `/models` + bundled synced catalog for the chatgpt-codex kind).

- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

AGENTS.md updated: the ChatGPT OAuth contract (one identity per auth domain, rename keeps the entry) and the model-list dispatch (codex `/models` + bundled synced catalog for the chatgpt-codex kind).

- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. - **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

AGENTS.md updated: the ChatGPT OAuth contract (one identity per auth domain, rename keeps the entry) and the model-list dispatch (codex `/models` + bundled synced catalog for the chatgpt-codex kind).

Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8.
