# pr-1708: fix(1706): codex auth single provider identity + full model list

## Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1708
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1708
- **Title**: fix(1706): codex auth single provider identity + full model list
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1706-codex-auth-provider-naming` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +342
- **Deletions**: -151
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

AGENTS.md updated: the ChatGPT OAuth contract (one identity per auth domain, rename keeps the entry) and the model-list dispatch (codex `/models` + bundled synced catalog for the chatgpt-codex kind).

# Pull Request Information

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.

# pr-1708: fix(1706): codex auth single provider identity + full model list

## Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

# Pull Request Information

- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1708
- **Title**: fix(1706): codex auth single provider identity + full model list
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1706-codex-auth-provider-naming` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +342
- **Deletions**: -151
- **Created**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

AGENTS.md updated: the ChatGPT OAuth contract (one identity per auth domain, rename keeps the entry) and the model-list dispatch (codex `/models` + bundled synced catalog for the chatgpt-codex kind).

- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7

- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T10:39:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1706 (does not close — linking for traceability; close on the issue side when verified).

## Root causes (the three from the issue)

1. **Second codex auth minted a parallel entry.** The OAuth save path resolves the existing same-domain record first (base URL via `_entryForBaseUrl`, alias spelling via `_entryForCanonicalName`), but the provider-name step treated any typed name as a NEW account boundary: `registry.find(newName) == null` → `registry.add(...)` — a second entry. First add named `chatgpt.com` (the host-derived default), second add with a custom name → two `/provider` rows for one ChatGPT account.
2. **Custom name vs `chatgpt` identity.** Same mint path: a custom-named record became a parallel provider identity instead of a label on the one chatgpt domain record (the `/provider kimi routes-to-catalog` convention: one identity per built-in provider).
3. **Model list showed only the model picked at add time.** The `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) had NO chatgpt-codex branch — the dispatch fell through to `_fetchOpenAiShapeIds`, which answers `[]` for the codex dialect (`api: responses`, not `openai-completions`). The cache then held the single-id last-resort seed (`entry.modelId`): exactly one model.

## Fixes

1. `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials` (lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart): when a same-domain record exists, the login lands ON it. A typed name RENAMES the record (the edit wizard's rename shape: drop old record, save under the new name; creds go to the new name-scoped key slot), and the guided model pick re-runs. Enter keeps name + model (re-auth in place — unchanged). The account picker's "add another account" became "sign in again (re-auth)".
2. `CustomProviderRegistry` load merge (lib/src/cli/custom_providers.dart): for the chatgpt-codex backend the AUTH DOMAIN is the identity — a custom-named record and the derived `chatgpt.com` spelling fold onto one entry at config load (union keeps key slot/model, merge note printed). Other providers keep name-based identities (kimi/dial legitimately host several same-endpoint accounts). The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start.
3. `_fetchIdsForProvider` (lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart) gained the chatgpt-codex branch: the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes — `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models` under the account's OAuth blob (verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs` + `codex-api/src/endpoint/models.rs`: `{CHATGPT_CODEX_BASE_URL}/models`, `ModelsResponse{models:[{slug,…}]}`) — via the existing `_CodexDialect` (`fetchModelsForEndpoint`), whose bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels` from `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart` ← codex-rs models.json) answers whenever the endpoint can't, so the picker lists the full catalog (8 slugs today), never fewer than the live answer.

## Test evidence (standalone SDK in the worktree; shared host dart is SIGKilled)

- `dart analyze` on all touched files: **No issues found**.
- `dart test test/cli/agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_model_test.dart test/cli/custom_providers_test.dart` → **68 passing, 0 failing**, including:
  - rewritten `a second codex auth re-auths the same identity (#1706: rename, never a twin entry)` — two OAuth rounds (`work` → `personal`) end with ONE entry named `personal`, blob in its name-scoped slot;
  - rewritten `a new name on a second auth renames the entry and re-picks its model (#1706)` — guided pick lands on the renamed single record;
  - unchanged `re-auth to the SAME entry keeps its model` (Enter path intact) and `a same-named entry on a different backend never receives the login` (domain-constrained alias resolution intact);
  - new `#1706: a custom-named codex record folds onto the chatgpt domain` (load merge) + `different-endpoint providers keep their own identities` (fold is codex-specific);
  - new `a saved chatgpt entry lists the codex /models answer (#1706)` — the picker refresh hits `{base}/models` and the codex row lists the live ids (plus the saved id, per the documented union) instead of the single seed.
- Adjacent suites green: `agent_cli_provider_test.dart` (118), `settings_flow_test.dart` (106), `copilot_provider_test.dart` + `llm_relay_sec_test.dart` (41), `roles_custom_providers_boot_test.dart` + `provider_key_lifecycle_test.dart` + `aiin_provider_commands_test.dart` (21), `provider_export_test.dart`, `add_provider_picker_test.dart`, `models_for_endpoint_test.dart`, `fresh_install_provider_flow_test.dart`.
- `dart format` applied to all touched Dart files.

Confirmed the persistence path:
- `persistConfig` → `saveCliConfig(home, saved.copyWith(customProviders: cli.config.customProviders?.entries ?? saved.customProviders, ...))`.
- `saveCliConfig` → `_mergeWithOnDisk` → `mergeCustomProviderEntries(callerEntries, onDiskEntries)` — a NAME-keyed union: on-disk entries not in the caller's name set survive.

So with the new domain-based load fold:
1. Disk: `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` (both apiType chatgpt, same baseUrl).
2. Boot: `CustomProviderRegistry(entries)` folds → in-memory `[my-codex]` + mergeNote printed.
3. ANY persistConfig (boot calls it unconditionally! gh-1572 — `try { await persistConfig(); }` right at the end of the wiring): caller = `[my-codex]`, onDisk = `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` → merged = `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` → written back to disk unchanged (both records persist).
4. Next boot: fold again → note prints again. Forever.

1. Disk: `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` (both apiType chatgpt, same baseUrl).
2. Boot: `CustomProviderRegistry(entries)` folds → in-memory `[my-codex]` + mergeNote printed.

So with the new domain-based load fold:
1. Disk: `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` (both apiType chatgpt, same baseUrl).
2. Boot: `CustomProviderRegistry(entries)` folds → in-memory `[my-codex]` + mergeNote printed.
3. ANY persistConfig (boot calls it unconditionally! gh-1572 — `try { await persistConfig(); }` right at the end of the wiring): caller = `[my-codex]`, onDisk = `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` → merged = `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` → written back to disk unchanged (both records persist).
4. Next boot: fold again → note prints again. Forever.

So the "owner's existing duplicate heals on next start" claim is only HALF true: the /provider picker shows one row (in-memory), but the duplicate record is never removed from config.yaml, and the merge note ("merged duplicate provider record ... (same auth domain)") reprints on EVERY boot. The intended behavior was surely "heals on next start" — the duplicate disappears from the file (like the reserved ghost case, which heals because mergeCustomProviderEntries drops reserved names from BOTH lists).

Hmm wait — let me double-check: does boot really call persistConfig unconditionally? Yes: `try { await persistConfig(); }` right after the assignment (gh-1572 note: "boot calls the save unconditionally — an unchanged save must not touch the file"). And `saveCliConfig` skips the write when `finalText == diskText`. In the duplicate case, merged = both entries (unchanged), so finalText == diskText → NO write. Fine — the file keeps both; next boot re-folds, note reprints.

So the observable user impact: the fold is cosmetic-per-boot; the note nags every boot; the twin keeps living in config.yaml. If the user hand-edits the twin to drop it, fine, but the tool never heals the file. Confirmed the persistence path:
- `persistConfig` → `saveCliConfig(home, saved.copyWith(customProviders: cli.config.customProviders?.entries ?? saved.customProviders, ...))`.
- `saveCliConfig` → `_mergeWithOnDisk` → `mergeCustomProviderEntries(callerEntries, onDiskEntries)` — a NAME-keyed union: on-disk entries not in the caller's name set survive.

So with the new domain-based load fold:
1. Disk: `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` (both apiType chatgpt, same baseUrl).
2. Boot: `CustomProviderRegistry(entries)` folds → in-memory `[my-codex]` + mergeNote printed.
3. ANY persistConfig (boot calls it unconditionally! gh-1572 — `try { await persistConfig(); }` right at the end of the wiring): caller = `[my-codex]`, onDisk = `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` → merged = `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` → written back to disk unchanged (both records persist).
4. Next boot: fold again → note prints again. Forever.

1. Disk: `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` (both apiType chatgpt, same baseUrl).
2. Boot: `CustomProviderRegistry(entries)` folds → in-memory `[my-codex]` + mergeNote printed.

(same auth domain)") reprints on EVERY boot. Confirmed the persistence path:
- `persistConfig` → `saveCliConfig(home, saved.copyWith(customProviders: cli.config.customProviders?.entries ?? saved.customProviders, ...))`.
- `saveCliConfig` → `_mergeWithOnDisk` → `mergeCustomProviderEntries(callerEntries, onDiskEntries)` — a NAME-keyed union: on-disk entries not in the caller's name set survive.

So with the new domain-based load fold:
1. Disk: `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` (both apiType chatgpt, same baseUrl).
2. Boot: `CustomProviderRegistry(entries)` folds → in-memory `[my-codex]` + mergeNote printed.
3. ANY persistConfig (boot calls it unconditionally! gh-1572 — `try { await persistConfig(); }` right at the end of the wiring): caller = `[my-codex]`, onDisk = `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` → merged = `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` → written back to disk unchanged (both records persist).
4. Next boot: fold again → note prints again. Forever.

So the "owner's existing duplicate heals on next start" claim is only HALF true: the /provider picker shows one row (in-memory), but the duplicate record is never removed from config.yaml, and the merge note ("merged duplicate provider record ... (same auth domain)") reprints on EVERY boot. The intended behavior was surely "heals on next start" — the duplicate disappears from the file (like the reserved ghost case, which heals because mergeCustomProviderEntries drops reserved names from BOTH lists).

Hmm wait — let me double-check: does boot really call persistConfig unconditionally? Yes: `try { await persistConfig(); }` right after the assignment (gh-1572 note: "boot calls the save unconditionally — an unchanged save must not touch the file"). And `saveCliConfig` skips the write when `finalText == diskText`. In the duplicate case, merged = both entries (unchanged), so finalText == diskText → NO write. Fine — the file keeps both; next boot re-folds, note reprints.

So the observable user impact: the fold is cosmetic-per-boot; the note nags every boot; the twin keeps living in config.yaml. If the user hand-edits the twin to drop it, fine, but the tool never heals the file. Also — the merge note printing every boot contradicts the doc comment "(a ghost-first load swaps both...)" — actually the ghost case does heal on disk (reserved names are filtered from the merged result). But the new codex fold does NOT heal.

Is this BLOCKING or IMPORTANT? The PR's stated fix #2: "the CustomProviderRegistry load merge for chatgpt-codex folds existing same-domain records onto ONE entry at load". The load fold works in memory. The PR description says "The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start." — that's the AC. Does it heal? In the picker, yes (one row). On disk, no — the duplicate survives every write-back. Hmm, wait — actually let me re-check: does the on-disk twin survive? `mergeCustomProviderEntries` keeps on-disk entries whose NAME is not in callerNames. The twin's name is `chatgpt.com`, caller names = {my-codex}. So yes, the twin survives.

BUT WAIT — I should double check the owner repro order: "codex auth added twice — once under a custom name, once under the derived chatgpt.com". The derived name comes from `_codeMieHostName(spec.defaultBaseUrl)` → likely `chatgpt.com`. So disk = [chatgpt.com, my-custom]. After fold, in-memory = [chatgpt.com] (first comes first, custom folds onto it — unless ghost rules). Save back: caller=[chatgpt.com], onDisk=[chatgpt.com, my-custom] → my-custom survives → disk keeps both. Same conclusion.

Is this worth a BLOCKING? Severity calibration: BLOCKING = broken behavior/red CI/scope violation/security/data loss. The declared AC "the owner's existing duplicate heals on next start" — in-memory it does; on disk it doesn't. The user-visible symptom (two /provider rows both marked current) IS fixed because the picker reads the in-memory registry. The residual: (a) the fold note reprints on every boot (nag), (b) config.yaml keeps the stale twin forever — and if the fold note ever says "merged X onto Y", a user might expect X gone from the file. Also (c) — more subtle — the /provider write-back keeps a stale twin whose modelId/keyName may be outdated; but the registry ignores it at load, so harmless beyond noise.

Hmm, actually there's one more scenario where it matters: the RESURRECTED twin is a full entry — if the user later EDITS the surviving entry's baseUrl via the edit wizard (changing it away from chatgpt.com), the twin (old baseUrl) is still on disk and now has a DIFFERENT identity than the survivor → on next load, the twin no longer folds → TWO codex entries again, and possibly the twin becomes "current" or lists twice. Edge-of-edge.

I'd classify this as IMPORTANT (⚠️), phrased as: the write-back merge (`mergeCustomProviderEntries`) is name-keyed, so the folded-away twin is re-persisted on every config save — the duplicate never leaves config.yaml and the merge note reprints on every boot; consider folding in `mergeCustomProviderEntries` too (identity-keyed, or dropping on-disk entries whose identity matches a caller entry).

blocks.text:
Confirmed the persistence path:
- `persistConfig` → `saveCliConfig(home, saved.copyWith(customProviders: cli.config.customProviders?.entries ?? saved.customProviders, ...))`.
- `saveCliConfig` → `_mergeWithOnDisk` → `mergeCustomProviderEntries(callerEntries, onDiskEntries)` — a NAME-keyed union: on-disk entries not in the caller's name set survive.

So with the new domain-based load fold:
1. Disk: `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` (both apiType chatgpt, same baseUrl).
2. Boot: `CustomProviderRegistry(entries)` folds → in-memory `[my-codex]` + mergeNote printed.
3. ANY persistConfig (boot calls it unconditionally! gh-1572 — `try { await persistConfig(); }` right at the end of the wiring): caller = `[my-codex]`, onDisk = `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` → merged = `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` → written back to disk unchanged (both records persist).
4. Next boot: fold again → note prints again. Forever.

So the "owner's existing duplicate heals on next start" claim is only HALF true: the /provider picker shows one row (in-memory), but the duplicate record is never removed from config.yaml, and the merge note ("merged duplicate provider record ... (same auth domain)") reprints on EVERY boot. The intended behavior was surely "heals on next start" — the duplicate disappears from the file (like the reserved ghost case, which heals because mergeCustomProviderEntries drops reserved names from BOTH lists).

Hmm wait — let me double-check: does boot really call persistConfig unconditionally? Yes: `try { await persistConfig(); }` right after the assignment (gh-1572 note: "boot calls the save unconditionally — an unchanged save must not touch the file"). And `saveCliConfig` skips the write when `finalText == diskText`. In the duplicate case, merged = both entries (unchanged), so finalText == diskText → NO write. Fine — the file keeps both; next boot re-folds, note reprints.

So the observable user impact: the fold is cosmetic-per-boot; the note nags every boot; the twin keeps living in config.yaml. If the user hand-edits the twin to drop it, fine, but the tool never heals the file. Also — the merge note printing every boot contradicts the doc comment "(a ghost-first load swaps both...)" — actually the ghost case does heal on disk (reserved names are filtered from the merged result). But the new codex fold does NOT heal.

Is this BLOCKING or IMPORTANT? The PR's stated fix #2: "the CustomProviderRegistry load merge for chatgpt-codex folds existing same-domain records onto ONE entry at load". The load fold works in memory. The PR description says "The owner's existing duplicate heals on next start." — that's the AC. Does it heal? In the picker, yes (one row). On disk, no — the duplicate survives every write-back. Hmm, wait — actually let me re-check: does the on-disk twin survive? `mergeCustomProviderEntries` keeps on-disk entries whose NAME is not in callerNames. The twin's name is `chatgpt.com`, caller names = {my-codex}. So yes, the twin survives.

BUT WAIT — I should double check the owner repro order: "codex auth added twice — once under a custom name, once under the derived chatgpt.com". The derived name comes from `_codeMieHostName(spec.defaultBaseUrl)` → likely `chatgpt.com`. So disk = [chatgpt.com, my-custom]. After fold, in-memory = [chatgpt.com] (first comes first, custom folds onto it — unless ghost rules). Save back: caller=[chatgpt.com], onDisk=[chatgpt.com, my-custom] → my-custom survives → disk keeps both. Same conclusion.

Is this worth a BLOCKING? Severity calibration: BLOCKING = broken behavior/red CI/scope violation/security/data loss. The declared AC "the owner's existing duplicate heals on next start" — in-memory it does; on disk it doesn't. The user-visible symptom (two /provider rows both marked current) IS fixed because the picker reads the in-memory registry. The residual: (a) the fold note reprints on every boot (nag), (b) config.yaml keeps the stale twin forever — and if the fold note ever says "merged X onto Y", a user might expect X gone from the file. Also (c) — more subtle — the /provider write-back keeps a stale twin whose modelId/keyName may be outdated; but the registry ignores it at load, so harmless beyond noise.

Hmm, actually there's one more scenario where it matters: the RESURRECTED twin is a full entry — if the user later EDITS the surviving entry's baseUrl via the edit wizard (changing it away from chatgpt.com), the twin (old baseUrl) is still on disk and now has a DIFFERENT identity than the survivor → on next load, the twin no longer folds → TWO codex entries again, and possibly the twin becomes "current" or lists twice. Edge-of-edge.

I'd classify this as IMPORTANT (⚠️), phrased as: the write-back merge (`mergeCustomProviderEntries`) is name-keyed, so the folded-away twin is re-persisted on every config save — the duplicate never leaves config.yaml and the merge note reprints on every boot; consider folding in `mergeCustomProviderEntries` too (identity-keyed, or dropping on-disk entries whose identity matches a caller entry).

Wait — but hold on. Let me check `mergeCustomProviderEntries` more carefully — maybe there's already identity handling. No:

```dart
List<CustomProviderEntry> mergeCustomProviderEntries(

     if (!callerNames.contains(e.name.toLowerCase()) &&
         !isReservedCustomProviderName(e.name))
       e,
 ];
}
``

Pure name-keyed. The PR did NOT touch this function. So yes — the twin resurrects on disk (well, never leaves).

Hmm, but actually — WAIT. Is this actually pre-existing behavior for the #706 alias case? For #706, the ghost `chatgpt` (reserved) is filtered from on-disk too, so the ghost heals. The alias `chatgpt.com` vs `chatgpt` — `chatgpt` is reserved → dropped. So #706's heal-on-disk worked only because the twin was RESERVED. The new #1706 twins are NOT reserved names (custom name + `chatgpt.com`). `chatgpt.com` — is it reserved? `isReservedCustomProviderName('chatgpt.com')` → `providerCatalog.containsKey('chatgpt.com')` → the catalog key is `chatgpt`, not `chatgpt.com` → NOT reserved. Good — `_askConnectProviderName`:
- Reserved (catalog) names rejected with re-prompt.
- Unusable names re-prompt.
- Clash with an entry of a DIFFERENT baseUrl retries unless allowClash (here only `clash == existing` allowed). Note: `clash.baseUrl != sameBaseUrl` — sameBaseUrl = spec.defaultBaseUrl. BUT — wait, one subtle thing: the clash check uses `find(name)` which is alias-aware (`find('chatgpt')` canonicalizes to 'chatgpt' and matches `chatgpt.com` entries... hmm, actually find's second loop canonicalizes both sides via canonicalProviderName; `canonicalProviderName('chatgpt.com') = 'chatgpt'`). Now, what about the case where the typed name matches the SAME baseUrl entry but under an alias spelling — that IS `existing` (already resolved) — allowed. OK.

Now — the case-sensitivity thing: `name != existing.name` is case-SENSITIVE. Typing 'Personal' vs existing 'personal' → treated as rename; removeWhere drops 'personal'; add creates 'Personal'. `find` is case-insensitive so `find('Personal')` would have found 'personal'... but the keyName resolution happens after removeWhere: `registry?.find(name)?.keyName` — 'personal' was already removed → null → fresh slot FA_KEY_CHATGPT_COM_PERSONAL (uppercase 'Personal' → keyNameFor probably uppercases). Now the `sameAccount` check: `existing != null && name == existing.name` — case-sensitive; 'Personal' vs 'personal' → treated as rename → guided model pick re-runs. Cosmetic.

(same auth domain)") reprints on EVERY boot. And `saveCliConfig` skips the write when `finalText == diskText`. In the duplicate case, merged = both entries (unchanged), so finalText == diskText → NO write. Fine — the file keeps both; next boot re-folds, note reprints.

So the observable user impact: the fold is cosmetic-per-boot; the note nags every boot; the twin keeps living in config.yaml. Confirmed the persistence path:
- `persistConfig` → `saveCliConfig(home, saved.copyWith(customProviders: cli.config.customProviders?.entries ?? saved.customProviders, ...))`.
- `saveCliConfig` → `_mergeWithOnDisk` → `mergeCustomProviderEntries(callerEntries, onDiskEntries)` — a NAME-keyed union: on-disk entries not in the caller's name set survive.

So with the new domain-based load fold:
1. Disk: `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` (both apiType chatgpt, same baseUrl).
2. Boot: `CustomProviderRegistry(entries)` folds → in-memory `[my-codex]` + mergeNote printed.
3. ANY persistConfig (boot calls it unconditionally! gh-1572 — `try { await persistConfig(); }` right at the end of the wiring): caller = `[my-codex]`, onDisk = `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` → merged = `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` → written back to disk unchanged (both records persist).
4. Next boot: fold again → note prints again. Forever.

So the "owner's existing duplicate heals on next start" claim is only HALF true: the /provider picker shows one row (in-memory), but the duplicate record is never removed from config.yaml, and the merge note ("merged duplicate provider record ... (same auth domain)") reprints on EVERY boot. The intended behavior was surely "heals on next start" — the duplicate disappears from the file (like the reserved ghost case, which heals because mergeCustomProviderEntries drops reserved names from BOTH lists).

Hmm wait — let me double-check: does boot really call persistConfig unconditionally? Yes: `try { await persistConfig(); }` right after the assignment (gh-1572 note: "boot calls the save unconditionally — an unchanged save must not touch the file"). And `saveCliConfig` skips the write when `finalText == diskText`. In the duplicate case, merged = both entries (unchanged), so finalText == diskText → NO write. Fine — the file keeps both; next boot re-folds, note reprints.

So the observable user impact: the fold is cosmetic-per-boot; the note nags every boot; the twin keeps living in config.yaml. If the user hand-edits the twin to drop it, fine, but the tool never heals the file. Also — the merge note printing every boot contradicts the doc comment "(a ghost-first load swaps both...)" — actually the ghost case does heal on disk (reserved names are filtered from the merged result). But the new codex fold does NOT heal.

Is this BLOCKING or IMPORTANT? The PR's stated fix #2: "the CustomProviderRegistry load merge for chatgpt-codex folds existing same-domain records onto ONE entry at load". on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated

publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT — a rename orphans the old name-scoped key slot holding a live OAuth blob

The record is dropped here and the fresh blob is written to the new name-scoped
slot, but nothing deletes `FA_KEY_CHATGPT_COM_<OLD>` — the prior grant's
access+refresh tokens stay in the secure store with no registry pointer (only
`/key delete <old>` reaches them). This matches the edit wizard's rename shape,
so it's consistent with the repo convention — but for OAuth blobs (unlike API
keys) the stale slot keeps a *live grant* alive, and the old multi-account test
that asserted slot retention was removed along with multi-account itself.
Cleanup of the old slot on rename, or a printed `/key delete <old slot>` hint,
would close the loop. (The write-back half of this — the dropped record also
surviving the persist merge — is covered in the `_recordIdentity` comment.)

# 💡 SUGGESTION — the comment promises coverage the body doesn't deliver

The comment says "a kimi and an openai entry one host stay separate records …
and two chatgpt records on different endpoints never merge", but the body only
builds two **openai** entries with *different names* — plain name-based
identity keeps those apart regardless of this PR. The load-bearing case for the
new fold — two chatgpt-codex entries with **different baseUrls** staying
separate — is the one left untested (it does hold; verified this run). Worth
asserting directly, since it's the invariant that keeps a codex proxy entry
from being absorbed into the chatgpt.com record.

This fold is load-only. The persist path re-attaches every on-disk entry whose
*name* the caller no longer carries: `saveCliConfig` → `_mergeWithOnDisk` →
`mergeCustomProviderEntries` (cli_config.dart:1864, custom_providers.dart:249)
is a name-keyed union, so the folded-away `chatgpt.com` twin survives every
write-back and `mergeNotes.forEach(stderr.writeln)` (bin/fah_runapp.dart:1408)
prints `merged duplicate provider record "chatgpt.com" onto … (same auth domain)`
on **every** boot. Verified this run by executing the repo's own functions:

- load fold of `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]` (same baseUrl) → `[my-codex]` + note
- persist merge of that caller with the same on-disk list → `[my-codex, chatgpt.com]`
- second boot → identical note again

survives the write-back and the next load re-folds it — the picker stays clean
(the user-visible #1706 symptom is fixed), but the duplicate never leaves the
file and the note is a permanent boot nag for exactly the user class this PR
targets ("the owner's existing duplicate heals on next start" only holds for
the picker view).

Could the write-back merge be identity-aware — e.g. drop on-disk entries whose

config.yaml actually heals and the note prints once?

The record is dropped here and the fresh blob is written to the new name-scoped

that asserted slot retention was removed along with multi-account itself.

write-back and `mergeNotes.forEach(stderr.writeln)` (bin/fah_runapp.dart:1408)
prints `merged duplicate provider record "chatgpt.com" onto … (same auth domain)`
on **every** boot. Verified this run by executing the repo's own functions:

targets ("the owner's existing duplicate heals on next start" only holds for
